summary: Shoshone County hump with a 1930s fire lookout cabin now described as ruins; sources give only the decade and disagree on the elevation.

facts.design: Fire lookout cabin on the ground, with no tower (1930s)
facts.status_note: Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts describe ruins; the Forest Fire Lookout Association list marks the site gone.

visit.trail_note: Listed as hike-in ruins by Idaho Fire Lookouts; Gaia GPS describes the Larkins Creek Trail as going by Mulligan Hump.

events.note: Fire lookout cabin; sources give only the 1930s

evidence.supports: Ten miles northwest of Canyon R.S.
Forest Fire Lookout Association list marks the site Ground Gone

evidence.quote: Mulligan Hump via Larkins Creek Trail
This is a moderate one way trail

evidence.supports: Moderate one-way trail that goes by the hump
evidence.quote: This trail goes by Mulligan Hump , Mud Lake , and Larkins Lake .

corrections.why: Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts both describe remains as ruins. The FFLA list's Gone is the only source that says the site is gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com gives 3,930 feet; Peakery gives 3,848 feet (1,173 m). The facts record no elevation; the story reports both figures.
The FFLA list says Gone; two other sources say ruins. Facts use ruins because it describes what is physically left on the ground.

sources.title: Mulligan Hump via Larkins Creek Trail

notes_for_editor: Thin record: two lookout-history pages with little detail, plus an elevation and status disagreement. The story gives the 1930s date as a decade only. Canyon R.S. is written as the source abbreviates it; it is likely a Forest Service ranger station but the expansion is not sourced. No staffing is recorded in any source, so staffing is omitted from facts and story. The Gaia GPS trail page is a hiking-route listing, not a land-manager source; whether the site is open to the public is not stated.
